topics.heading: SEC filings
topics.intro: sec.gov refuses automated requests whose User-Agent does not give a contact email address, and the project's scripts send none. `check_quotes.py` therefore does not fetch sec.gov and reports these rows as fetch failed. The quotes were checked in excerpts returned by a summarising web fetch, which is not a character-for-character comparison. Apple was compared character for character against a saved copy of the filing.

topics.heading: Date-arithmetic checks
topics.intro: Every check below is reproduced by [`research/verification/verify_claims.py`](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/fiscalclock/blob/main/research/verification/README.md), whose committed output is [`expected_output.txt`](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/fiscalclock/blob/main/research/verification/expected_output.txt). The docs workflow reruns it on every pull request and compares the output byte for byte.

topics.heading: Unverified claims
topics.intro: These four claims from the research documents have no authoritative source as of 1 Nov 2026. The wiki marks them unverified wherever they appear and does not rely on them for any requirement.
topics.outro: The Indian FY/AY claim was on this list in the plan (contradiction D10). It now has an official source, which corrects it (see [India, ERP and transition years](#india-erp-and-transition-years)).

claims.claim: India: FY 2025-26 and AY 2026-27 are two names for one year
claims.quote: the use of term 'assessment year' has been discontinued
claims.evidence: They are different years: AY 2026-27 is the year after FY 2025-26, in which its income is assessed. From 1 April 2026 the Income-tax Act, 2025 uses "tax year", and "the use of term 'assessment year' has been discontinued".
